glosses: Able to be expended; not inexhaustible.

examples.text: Oil and other expendable resources are frequently the subject of military disputes.

glosses: Designed for a single use; not reusable.

examples.text: The anti-aircraft rocket is fired from an expendable launch platform.

glosses: Not essential or mandatory in order to achieve a goal.

examples.text: The research department was deemed expendable, and its funding was not renewed.

glosses: Regarded as not worth preserving or saving; able to be sacrificed.

examples.text: In the internecine rivalries of large corporations, whole departments may become expendable in the execution of one executive's power play.
He was expendable, like commodities past their use.
The Taunton-Minehead line (now managed by the West Somerset Railway) was considered much more expendable.

glosses: An expendable person or object; usually used in the plural.

examples.text: Private Johnson was afraid the Lieutenant considered him an expendable, since he was always picked as point man.

glosses: Able to be done without; easily replaced.
Capable of being dispensed.

examples.text: The reward could be a preferred food, a sticker, blowing some bubbles, a noisemaker the child enjoys, a pat on the back, or some other easily dispensable reward that does not take the child away from the task at hand for more than a moment or two.

glosses: Subject to dispensation; possible to relax, exempt from, or annul.

examples.text: Jones' use of the term 'Ecclesiastical Law' in his definition of dispensations in Roman Catholic canon law points to the Roman Catholic distinction between divine law, from which no dispensation is possible, and merely ecclesiastical law, which is dispensable in certain circumstances.

glosses: Not essential to be taken in as part of an organism's diet, as it can be synthesized de novo.

examples.text: The difference in absorption rate is not surprising since whey has a high percentage of indispensable amino acids, which are absorbed more rapidly than dispensable amino acids.

glosses: Something that can reasonably be dispensed with; something unnecessary.
Qui fait l’objet d’un choix ; pour lequel on peut opter.

examples.text: Le latin est une matière optionnelle au collège qui devient facultative au lycée.
Certains réglages de ce programme sont optionnels.

glosses: Qui est en option, que l’on peut choisir secondairement (souvent à propos d’accessoires et particulièrement pour les automobiles).

examples.text: Cette splendide voiture possède en outre beaucoup d’équipements optionnels.

glosses: Qui laisse la faculté de faire ou de ne pas faire une chose ; dont on peut, à son gré, faire ou ne pas faire usage.

examples.text: D'autres champignons, les nécrotrophes, sont des saprophytes facultatifs. Ils peuvent se développer en tant que parasite sur les hôtes, puis continuer à vivre, croître et se multiplier sur les tissus morts de l'hôte après sa mort.
Cette disposition de la loi n’est que facultative.
Article facultatif.
Droit facultatif.
Épreuves d’examen facultatives.
Matières facultatives d’un programme d’études.

glosses: Pour lequel on peut accorder dispense.

glosses: Dont on peut se dispenser, se passer.
